subject: SEM with mix of categorical and continuous data?

messages.author: 7a5ef72865ecc0d0
messages.subject: SEM with mix of categorical and continuous data?
parts:
Hello all, I’m hoping to do a path analysis with several latent variables. The dataset is a mix of both categorial and continuous variables, with the outcome variable being a binary categorical variable (yes or no on substance use inititation). My questions:

  1. Should I be scaling all of the variables, or just the continuous ones?

  2. In lavaan, is it sufficient to input the categorical variables into the “ordered” command, or do I need to prepare them another way?

  3. It seems from my reading that WLSM is the best estimator/method, but when I call it for my final model fit, it raises a warning that I should not use it for continuous data

Any insights would be helpful. Take care!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: SEM with mix of categorical and continuous data?
parts: 1. Should I be scaling all of the variables, or just the continuous ones?
1. In lavaan, is it sufficient to input the categorical variables into the “ordered” command, or do I need to prepare them another way?
1. It seems from my reading that WLSM is the best estimator/method, but when I call it for my final model fit, it raises a warning that I should not use it for continuous data

For categorical data, the estimator is DWLS (diagonally weighted least squares).  The M(V) suffix is just a shortcut for indicating the type of test statistic you want.  When you specify any variables as ordered=, lavaan selects DWLS automatically, so there is no need to set it manually, unless you prefer unweighted (ULS) or pairwise maximum likelihood (PML) instead.  The default test= will be "scaled.shifted", which typically performs better than alternative adjustments.
